title: Kronauer's Masonic album (Vienna 1783-91, OeNB Cod. Ser. n. 4832): the entry on fol. 28r, 'Der freye Mensch aus meiner Republick', in an invented script of Georgian-looking letters

documents.shelfmark: Vienna, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Cod. Ser. n. 4832 (AC14378542), fol. 28r
documents.date: Oct. 178? (Vienna; last digit of the year disguised and not read; year field set from the album's dated cipher entry, fol. 31r, 25 Sep 1784)
documents.route: album entry for Johann Georg Kronauer

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the page, elsewhere in the album or in print as far as searched (catalogue 2836 vetting; Nettl 1957 prints only the clear entries).

transcription.source: ONB IIIF manifest 1004802B, canvas index 64 (full served size 1047 px) and 3-7x crops
transcription.notes: Two passes: pass A with the solve; pass B blind by a second agent that saw only the image and crops, with no hint on language or content. Codes as in pass B; differences arbitrated on the image (NOTES.md).

system.summary: Simple substitution of German letters by invented letter forms that look like Georgian Mkhedruli (the Georgian sound values are not used); one sign for b and p; enlarged forms for capitals; ä, ö, ü written ae, oe, ue; no q (bekuem); word division and punctuation kept.
system.notes: 37 types counting the capital forms apart (23 lower-case letters, 13 capitals, y). The other cipher entries of the album seen so far (fol. 24r, 31r) use square pigpen-type signs, a different system.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout chose Daniel Bourdeau's lead (catalogue 2836); the images were fetched by curl from the ONB IIIF service; transcription, solve and reading by the agent with no hints on the content.
tools: blind second solve by a separate agent

solution.what: ONB IIIF manifest 1004802B answered curl (with resets); all 188 canvases saved; fol. 28r = canvas index 64.
Glyph inventory and transcription of the heading, eight lines of text, place/date and signature from 3-7x crops (pass A).
Hand solve by word patterns: 'Kinder sind Kinder', '-er' endings, 'ist', 'sich', 'macht'; the key then read the whole page as German.

Blind second pass: a separate agent given only the image and crops (no language or content hint) built its own glyph inventory and reached the same key and the same text (differences: seinen/einen, gehöret/gehört, first word of the signature unread).
Read as continuous German prose (reading_f28r.md): 83 of 85 words read by sense; the surname and the year's last digit unresolved.

Catalogue 2836 vetting (DECODE, Tomokiyo, Lasry, Nettl 1957, Mozart documents), repository and our own folders searched for Kronauer, 4832, Stammbuch: no earlier reading. The album's member register (fol. 73v-77v) read in part: its numbers are not folios, so the signer was not identified.

outcome.fraction_read_source: reading_f28r.md: 85 words (heading 6, text 69, place/date 4, signature 6); 2 unresolved (surname, year), 11 probable counted read; 83/85 = 0.976
outcome.notes: No pre-registered held-out test: the page has about 400 signs and is the only text in this system in the album, and the key was built on the whole page. The check is a blind independent solve plus 75 words of continuous German, far beyond the unicity distance of a simple substitution. validation.tsv is ready for docs/_validate.py (de-1740s); it was not run here (no numpy on the contributor's machine).

gaps.item: surname of the signer ('Paul M…ll…ieur', 9 signs)
gaps.detail: letters read, no name fits; perhaps a pseudonym; the register entry 28 (v. Laibel) is not this leaf
digits disguised (7 turned, 8 plain); first and last signs alike

credits.note: lead: catalogue 2836 from the OeNB deep sweep, 15-16 Nov 2026

texts.label: Cod. Ser. n. 4832 fol. 28r, Vienna, Oct. 178?
texts.summary: A Rousseauist sketch, 'Der freye Mensch aus meiner Republick': man in a state of nature, without prince or senate, everything belonging to all, praising God through his conduct; signed 'Paul M…ll…ieur', Vienna, Oct. 178?.

reading_review.note: Contributor's own review, not a second human reader. A second transcription by a separate Opus session that saw only the image recovered the same key and text independently (differences: seinen/einen, gehöret/gehört, first word of the signature).
